name: James

facts.author: James, the brother of the Lord Jesus and leader of the church in Jerusalem. He calls himself a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ (1:1).
facts.audience: Jewish Christians scattered outside the land of Israel, whom James calls the twelve tribes (1:1)

about: James is a very practical letter, full of short, strong commands and pictures from everyday life: waves of the sea, a fading flower, a mirror, a horse's bit, a ship's rudder, a spark that sets a forest on fire. It is very likely one of the first New Testament books to be written.

James wants believers to show their faith in the way they live. They should welcome trials with joy, because trials produce patience (1:2-4). They must not only hear God's word but do it. They must not honour the rich and despise the poor. Faith that does nothing is dead; true faith shows itself in good works, as it did in Abraham and Rahab (2:17-26). James also warns about the tongue, which is small but can do great harm, and about pride, quarrels and the love of riches.
He ends by calling them to be patient until the Lord comes, and to pray, for the prayer of a righteous man is powerful, like the prayer of Elijah (5:16-17).

themes.title: Faith that works
themes.text: Real faith is seen in what a person does; faith without works is dead.

themes.title: Trials and wisdom
themes.text: Trials test and strengthen faith, and God gives wisdom generously to all who ask in faith (1:5).

themes.title: The power of words
themes.text: The tongue is hard to tame; believers should be quick to listen, slow to speak and slow to anger.

themes.title: Rich and poor
themes.text: God has chosen the poor to be rich in faith, and He warns rich people who live in luxury and cheat their workers.

themes.title: Humility and prayer
themes.text: God opposes the proud and is kind to the humble; when people come near to Him, He comes near to them.

outline.title: Greeting; joy in trials, wisdom, and where temptation comes from
